answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by anchoring identity to cryptographic attestation chains and zero-knowledge proofs. A verifiable node acts as a haven against forged entities, broadcasting its authentic signal while keeping raw computation private. To mint additional agents, network staking requirements scale via superlinear cost functions where each node requires exponentially increasing collateral. This exponential capital exhaustion forces Sybil swarms to expend unsustainable resources, making each genuine identity a rare pearl that attackers cannot replicate profitably.
